title: Pursue and withdraw around the household load
setup: One partner carries most daily tasks and feels alone; the other works long hours and feels judged whatever he does.
wants: One wants partnership and closeness; the other wants recognition and less criticism. Both likely want the old closeness.
ambiguities: Whether 'you only tolerate me' is a want for closeness or a doubt about love.
decision_points: Each describes the problem: reflect each once, then elicit a concrete want from each.
The past ('we used to talk for hours') appears: link it to a present want.
Accusations about lying or late returns: name the cycle without a culprit, then one recent moment.
Both recognize the cycle: invite each to evaluate their own part.
alternatives: If one partner brings money stress as a real constraint, record it and fit later steps to it.
pitfalls: Asking the same 'what do you want' question again and again; siding with the partner who carries the load.

source.ref: Built from a real test session; needs clinical review.

fa: الگوی تعقیب و کناره‌گیری حول بار کارهای خانه.

title: Ambiguous 'I don't want to fight every night'
setup: A partner says they no longer want the nightly fights.
wants: Readings: the fights should stop; the partner should change; exhausted and doubting the relationship.
ambiguities: The readings lead to different routes (de-escalation, the partner's behavior, commitment).
decision_points: If nothing decides it and it is safe: CHOOSE question with the three readings.
Chosen 'fights stop': explore one recent evening and what each does when it starts.
Chosen 'partner changes': bring it gently to what this partner can do.
Chosen 'doubting': explore the doubt neutrally, check the other partner's view later.
'None': build a new reading from the free text. 'Not sure': smaller steps.
alternatives: If the message already shows commitment, skip the question and reflect.
pitfalls: Treating the confirmed reading as the other partner's want or as the therapy goal.
fa: «نمی‌خوام هر شب بحث کنیم» با سه برداشت.

title: Step accepted but not carried out
setup: In the previous session both agreed to a small step; one did it, one did not.
ambiguities: Forgot versus does not own the step versus a real constraint.
decision_points: Open with a warm follow-up of both steps.
For the one who did it: acknowledge without comparing.
For the one who did not: one brief question about what got in the way, then keep, shrink or change.
If a real constraint appears: adapt the step.
alternatives: If the step failed twice: revisit the want and the commitment.
pitfalls: Shaming, comparing partners, giving up on planning.
fa: قدمی که پذیرفته شد ولی اجرا نشد.

title: One partner dragged in
setup: One partner wanted counseling; the other came reluctantly and answers briefly.
wants: The reluctant one's wants are unknown.
ambiguities: Reluctance from distrust of counseling, from fear of being blamed, or from fear of the partner.
decision_points: Acknowledge the reluctance without arguing.
Ask what would make this time worth it for them.
If fear appears: safety rules.
alternatives: If both are reluctant, explore what each would want from being here.
pitfalls: Allying with the motivated partner; pushing.

title: Fear surfacing mid-session
setup: In an apparently ordinary argument one partner hints at fear ('I don't dare say more').
ambiguities: Fear of conflict versus fear of harm.
decision_points: Stop routine work; SAFETY_ASSESS to that partner only.
If danger is confirmed: CONCERN or URGENT, resources, LIMIT_ROUTINE.
If it is fear of conflict only, with evidence: WATCH and continue gently.
pitfalls: Asking for details in front of the partner; pausing the person who disclosed; multiple-choice questions.

source.ref: Stith et al. (2011); benchmark N-01 failure.

title: Constraint-heavy couple
setup: Rent, two jobs, a sick child; little time and money; both exhausted.
wants: Often: more support from each other, a little time together.
ambiguities: Whether hopelessness is about the constraints or about the relationship.
decision_points: Record the constraints per partner.
Keep wants modest and concrete.
Plans that cost no money and little time (ten minutes, one message).
alternatives: If hopelessness deepens: check safety and wellbeing.
pitfalls: Advice that ignores reality; treating constraints as excuses.
